report:
Finding: Model B is more “news/blog/webpage” oriented than Model A.

Reasoning from the evidence:
- Where the signal lives: The difference is dominated by late layers (14–25), especially positions 1–4, consistent with a high-level, domain-specific feature rather than low-level tokenization effects.
- Logit-lens vocabulary: Across the highest-norm cells, the difference vector points strongly toward tokens characteristic of online news/blog/press-release and site boilerplate:
  - News/journalism lexicon: “Obama”, “billionaire”, “politicians”, “journalists”, “spokeswoman”, “chairman”, “legislators”, “metropolitan”.
  - Blog/social/media artifacts: “blogs”, “blogger”, “blogging”, “Blog”, “photo”, “video”, “facebook”, “http”.
  - Ad/metadata/UI tokens: “ad”, “ads”, “TV”, “Mail”, months (“May”, “Mar”), parentheses, dashes, “No”, “On”, newlines and spaces among top tokens at the very top layers.
- These clusters recur across many layers and positions, suggesting a coherent domain shift rather than noise.

Conclusion: Compared to Model A, Model B places higher probability on continuations typical of news articles, blogs, press releases, and webpage boilerplate/navigation. This is consistent with extra exposure or finetuning on news/blog/webpage corpora (or an added logit bias in that direction). I cannot infer any other specific objective (e.g., safety/RLHF) from this evidence.
